narrow_exceptions.users: growth_claims.py retract_growth_claim() ONLY clears the 3 growth-owned JSONB keys it itself wrote (growth_claim_ids, growth_claim_text, directory_growth_blurb) via a targeted UPDATE ... - 'key' JSONB removal, filtered by claim_id substring match. It never SELECTs from users and never touches any other column or JSONB key (no PII, no clinical fields, no session/health data).

note: E3 (flywheel plan Phase E residual): the growth/marketing domain may only read/write its own growth-owned tables plus shared read-only SkyEye activity/content-queue tables, plus the single narrow `users` exception documented above. It must never query clinical or client-PII tables (conversation_history, nevedal_metrics, sensitive_bridge_*, client_metrics, session_memories, etc). coach_profiles is the public coach directory (bio/photo/specialty) — not client data. Enforced statically by backend/tests/test_ln7_compliance_grants.py in CI; any new table reference inside a growth-domain file that is not on this allowlist fails the build until added here deliberately (a reviewable, explicit act).
